newsitem.title: USA: Bluesman Luther Allison dies at 57.
newsitem.headline: Bluesman Luther Allison dies at 57.

text.p: Award-winning blues star Luther Allison died on Tuesday, his record label said, one month after he had been diagnosed with inoperable lung cancer.

Allison, 57, died in Madison, Wisconsin, where he was being treated. He was diagnosed with terminal cancer on July 10 after suffering dizziness and a loss of coordination during a recent concert tour.

The Paris-based singer and guitar player had been promoting his latest album, "Reckless," for Alligator Records, which announced his death. The winner of three W.C. Handy Awards, Allison was born in Widener, Arkansas, on Aug. 17, 1939, and spent his formative musical years in Chicago.

In 1971 he became the first blues act to sign with Motown Records and recorded three albums for that label. He toured the United States in the 1970s before moving to Paris in the early 1980s, touring Europe and gaining blues superstar status there.
In 1994 he signed with Chicago-based Alligator label and had released two earlier albums there -- "Soul Fixin' Man" and 1995's "Blue Streak."

Many of his concert shows ran from three to four hours. During a North American tour earlier this year he appeared at the Beale Street Music Festival in Memphis, the Eureka Springs Blues Festival, the Montreal Jazz Festival, the Milwaukee Summerfest, the Monterey Bay Blues Festival and the Santa Cruz Blues Festival.
His latest album had been on Billboard's Blues Chart for 12 weeks and had topped the Living Blues Radio Charts since May.
Funeral services will be conducted on Saturday in Chicago.
